array.definition: A contiguous block of memory storing elements of identical data type accessible via integer indices.

dynamic array.definition: A variable-size list structure backed by a contiguous array that resizes automatically when capacity is reached.

dictionary.definition: An associative data structure that stores unique key-value pairs for constant or near-constant time lookups.

set.definition: An unordered collection of unique elements optimized for fast membership testing.

tuple.definition: An immutable, ordered sequence of elements stored in fixed contiguous memory locations.

design patterns.definition: Reusable, generalized solutions to common architectural and software design problems within a given context.

abstract data type.definition: A mathematical specification of a data structure that defines operations and behavior independently of any specific implementation.

iterator pattern.definition: A behavioral design pattern that provides a standardized mechanism to sequentially traverse elements of an aggregate object without exposing its internal representation.

factory pattern.definition: A creational design pattern that uses dedicated methods or objects to encapsulate element or structure creation logic.

strategy pattern.definition: A behavioral design pattern that encapsulates interchangeable algorithms into separate classes, allowing algorithmic behavior to be selected at runtime.

adapter pattern.definition: A structural design pattern that translates the interface of an existing class into another interface expected by a client.

singly linked list.definition: A linear data structure where each node contains a data field and a reference link to the next node in the sequence.

doubly linked list.definition: A linear data structure where each node contains data, a reference link to the next node, and a reference link to the previous node.

stack.definition: A linear data structure operating under a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) protocol.

queue.definition: A linear data structure operating under a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) protocol.

binary search tree.definition: A node-based binary tree data structure where the left subtree contains nodes with keys less than the node key, and the right subtree contains nodes with keys greater.

hash table.definition: A data structure that maps keys to values using a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets or slots.

time-space trade-off.definition: The principle where an algorithm or data structure reduces execution time at the cost of consuming additional memory, or vice versa.

priority queue.definition: An abstract data type where each element has an associated priority, and elements with higher priority are served before elements with lower priority.

cache locality.definition: The spatial or temporal proximity of memory accesses that enables efficient utilization of hardware cache memory.

asymptotic analysis.definition: A method of defining the limiting behavior of an algorithm's resource consumption as the input size approaches infinity.

worst-case time complexity.definition: The maximum execution time required by an algorithm over all possible inputs of size n.

best-case time complexity.definition: The minimum execution time required by an algorithm over all possible inputs of size n.

average-case time complexity.definition: The expected execution time required by an algorithm averaged over all possible inputs of size n.

auxiliary space.definition: The temporary or extra memory allocated by an algorithm during execution, excluding the space occupied by the input data.

recurrence relation.definition: An equation or inequality that defines a function in terms of its values on smaller inputs, used to analyze recursive algorithms.

Huffman coding.definition: A lossless data compression algorithm that constructs an optimal prefix code tree using a priority queue based on symbol frequencies.

prefix code.definition: A code system in which no valid code word is a prefix of any other valid code word, allowing unambiguous sequential decoding.

least recently used cache.definition: An in-memory caching mechanism that evicts the least recently accessed item when capacity is reached, implemented using a hash table and a doubly linked list.

inverted index.definition: A search index mapping distinct terms to lists of document identifiers or positions where those terms occur.

trie.definition: A tree-like search data structure used for efficient storage and retrieval of keys where nodes represent common prefixes.
